$comment: Inventory for docs/design/CSS-NATIVE-BUILTINS.md. One row per built-in colour/math function. `class` is one of: exact | exact-if | approx | already-css | none (defined in the design doc, section 1). `css` is the CSS-native form over the parameter names; `C`, `C1`, `C2` are colours, `A` an amount on the CSS channel scale, `N`, `B` numbers. `css` is the simplest CSS form (ladder rung 2), `extended` the longer one (rung 3); a `none` row reaches rung 4, compile time plus the JS runtime (doc §3.4a). `deferred` and `relativeDeferred` are the form an amount or places only the browser knows takes (Q2). A row with `aliasOf` is a second name for the row it names, with its classification. Every other registered function is listed in `outOfScope`; `packages/fns/src/__tests__/css-native-builtins.test.ts` checks the three lists cover the registries exactly.

functions.name: lighten
functions.css: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l + A, 100))
functions.relative: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l + l * A / 100, 100))
functions.deferred: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l + A / 1%, 100))
functions.relativeDeferred: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l + l * A / 1% / 100, 100))

functions.name: darken
functions.css: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l - A, 100))
functions.relative: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l - l * A / 100, 100))
functions.deferred: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l - A / 1%, 100))
functions.relativeDeferred: hsl(from C h s clamp(0, l - l * A / 1% / 100, 100))

functions.name: saturate
functions.css: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s + A, 100) l)
functions.relative: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s + s * A / 100, 100) l)
functions.deferred: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s + A / 1%, 100) l)
functions.relativeDeferred: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s + s * A / 1% / 100, 100) l)

functions.name: desaturate
functions.css: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s - A, 100) l)
functions.relative: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s - s * A / 100, 100) l)
functions.deferred: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s - A / 1%, 100) l)
functions.relativeDeferred: hsl(from C h clamp(0, s - s * A / 1% / 100, 100) l)

functions.name: spin
functions.css: hsl(from C calc(h + A) s l)

functions.name: fade
functions.css: rgb(from C r g b / A)
functions.deferred: rgb(from C r g b / calc(A / 100%))
functions.notes: A is an amount, a percentage whatever its unit: .5 is 0.005 and 50% is 0.5. What only the browser knows is converted to an alpha: a percentage goes in the slot as it is, a number of known type is its share of 100, and a value of no known type is taken to hold a percentage (Q2; owner: keep short form). A var() with a default, which an exposed variable reads as, of no known type stays in the slot as it is until the unit an exposed variable holds is ruled

functions.name: fadein
functions.css: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha + A))
functions.relative: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha + alpha * A))
functions.deferred: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha + A / 100%))
functions.relativeDeferred: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha + alpha * A / 100%))

functions.name: fadeout
functions.css: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha - A))
functions.relative: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha - alpha * A))
functions.deferred: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha - A / 100%))
functions.relativeDeferred: rgb(from C r g b / calc(alpha - alpha * A / 100%))

functions.name: mix
functions.notes: ruled 2026-11-01: color-mix(in srgb) for 0-100% (no legacy weighting); a weight outside 0-100% takes the relative form when one colour is known, else rung 4 (compile time + JS runtime; naming no export it fails). A colour written with none stays in the form. built: slice 8, stage 2, on one code path with Less mix; Sass's alpha-weighted result is replaced, per Q1
functions.extended: rgb(from C clamp(0, (r * alpha * w + q_r) / (alpha * w + p), 255) ... / calc(alpha * w + p)), w the share of the colour not known, p and q the known colour's opacity and premultiplied channels

functions.name: tint
functions.notes: rung 2 color-mix() for 0-100%; rung 3 relative rgb for a known weight outside 0-100%, exact for every weight, with the alpha terms color-mix() uses
functions.extended: rgb(from C clamp(0, (r * alpha * w + q_r) / (alpha * w + p), 255) ... / calc(alpha * w + p)), w the share of the colour not known, p and q the known colour's opacity and premultiplied channels

functions.name: shade
functions.notes: as tint, toward black
functions.extended: rgb(from C clamp(0, (r * alpha * w + q_r) / (alpha * w + p), 255) ... / calc(alpha * w + p)), w the share of the colour not known, p and q the known colour's opacity and premultiplied channels

functions.name: average
functions.notes: ruled 2026-11-01: mix() is color-mix(in srgb), compile-time results included (no legacy weighting); takes no weight

functions.name: hsv
functions.notes: exact for S and V in 0-100%, where white + black <= 100%: W = (1 - s)v and B = 1 - v, computed from a known S and V. Outside it a known input computes what hwb() does: a negative reads 0 and a sum over 100% normalizes to grey. A deferred S or V is taken to hold a percentage (Q2): W = calc((1 - S / 100%) * V), or calc(share * V) over a known S, and B = calc(100% - V)

functions.name: hsva
functions.notes: exact for S and V in 0-100%, where white + black <= 100%: W = (1 - s)v and B = 1 - v, computed from a known S and V. Outside it a known input computes what hwb() does: a negative reads 0 and a sum over 100% normalizes to grey. A deferred S or V is taken to hold a percentage (Q2): W = calc((1 - S / 100%) * V), or calc(share * V) over a known S, and B = calc(100% - V). A deferred A goes in the slot as it is

functions.name: rgba
functions.css: rgb(from C r g b / A)
functions.notes: the 2-slot (colour, alpha) overload, when C is a colour by type and either slot is deferred: rgba(currentcolor, .5), rgba(#000, var(--a)). rgba(var(--rgb), .5) and rgba(var(--c), var(--a)) are the CSS channel-list idiom and stay as written. 3+ slots are CSS already

functions.name: rgb
functions.notes: 3+ slots and one colour; its 2-slot overload is as Less rgba. A var() in a slot prints as written, and a known channel or alpha beside it is converted to what the compile reads there: rgb(var(--r), 1px, 0) is rgb(var(--r), 1, 0). An exposed variable in a channel prints over its var(), its unit divided out (calc(var(--r, 2px) / 1px)); an exposed colour is that var()

functions.name: hsl
functions.notes: 3+ slots and one colour. A var() in a slot prints as written, and a known slot beside it is converted to what the compile reads there: a hue in degrees, a unitless saturation or lightness a fraction of 1, clamped (hsl(var(--h), 50, 50) is hsl(var(--h), 100%, 100%)). An exposed variable prints over its var(), converted the same way

functions.name: hsla
functions.notes: as Less hsl

functions.name: multiply
functions.notes: per-channel product of two colours; relative colour syntax has one origin

functions.name: contrast
functions.withColors: rgb(from contrast-color(C) calc(Dr + (Lr - Dr) * r / 255) calc(Dg + (Lg - Dg) * r / 255) calc(Db + (Lb - Db) * r / 255) / calc(Da + (La - Da) * r / 255))
functions.notes: built: slice 7. Ruled 2026-11-01 (Q13): a known input picks dark/light by the larger WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio, so contrast(#999) = black; an explicit threshold keeps the luma rule for a known input and has no CSS form for an unknown one (it fails, or runs on the runtime). A lone contrast(<unknown>) goes by where it stands: directly in filter or backdrop-filter it is CSS's filter function, directly in any other declaration contrast-color(), and where no position is known as written (owner 2026-11-05 for grayscale and invert; the coordinator's extension to contrast). A number stays the filter. Black and white agree with contrast-color() in Chrome 152 on every origin of the grid; a custom pair can disagree, because the form switches where black and white do. Dark and light must be known for the withColors form

functions.name: hue
functions.notes: channel readers exist in CSS only as channel keywords inside a relative colour

functions.name: argb
functions.notes: returns #AARRGGBB text

functions.name: color
functions.notes: parses a string

functions.name: percentage
functions.notes: N a <number>

functions.name: abs
functions.notes: Over a number only the browser knows, a call prints this function, under the name after any namespace (built: slice 8, stage 3)

functions.name: ceil
functions.notes: N a <number>; a dimension needs B in N's unit, for a deferred N the unit its structure gives (`var(--x) + 1px`), else a number (Q3)

functions.name: round
functions.notes: Less P is decimal places, CSS B is a step; CSS nearest breaks ties toward +infinity, Less (V8) away from zero, hence sign/abs. N is not a decimal tie: the compile rounds round(1.005, 2) in base 10 to 1.01, browser floats give 1 (V8 open sub-question). A known N with a unit and a deferred P multiplies the step by 1 in that unit

functions.name: mod
functions.notes: Less mod is JS %, sign of the dividend = CSS rem(); CSS mod() takes the divisor's sign. Both arguments must share a type in CSS

functions.name: min
functions.notes: Less coerces a unitless argument; CSS needs consistent types. Over a number only the browser knows, a call prints this function, under the name after any namespace (built: slice 8, stage 3)

functions.name: invert
functions.css: rgb(from C calc(255 - r) calc(255 - g) calc(255 - b))
functions.weighted: color-mix(in srgb, rgb(from C calc(255 - r) calc(255 - g) calc(255 - b)) W%, C)
functions.notes: the inverted colour keeps C's alpha, so the weighted mix is exact. built: slice 8, stage 2. A known input computes through this form. A lone call over an unknown: directly in filter or backdrop-filter it is CSS's filter function, directly in any other declaration the form, and where no position is known (a variable, a mixin argument, inside another function) as written (owner 2026-11-05, Q13). A number stays the filter. color.invert(C) always takes the form; a weight makes it a colour by arity

functions.name: color.adjust
functions.css: rgb(from C clamp(0, r + R, 255) g b), hsl(from C calc(h + H) clamp(0, s + S, 100) clamp(0, l + L, 100)), hwb(from C h calc(w + W) calc(b + B))
functions.notes: built: slice 8, stage 4. One relative colour for the call: a named channel fills its slot, the others print their keywords. A known input computes through this form; an amount only the browser knows takes it too, as a percentage on a 0-100 channel

functions.name: color.scale
functions.css: hsl(from C h s calc(l + (100 - l) * F))
functions.notes: built: slice 8, stage 4. One relative colour for the call. F known: its sign picks the formula (positive: calc(l + (100 - l) * F), negative: calc(l + l * F)). F only the browser knows has no form, and fails
